## Work Order 1 — Security Fix: Gate team member-management tools on `team.manage_members`

### What was changed (10 files)

**Source code (8 files — 5 code changes per Work Order 1):**

| # | File | Change |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | `src/mem_mcp/auth/permissions.py` | Added all 7 catalog roles (`owner`, `admin`, `member`, `service-bot`, `viewer`, `vendor`, `customer`) to `ROLE_PERMISSIONS`. Legacy `admin`/`member`/`viewer` keys serve double-duty for both `team_role_assignments` and `team_members` fallback. Namespace disjointness enforced: no team role grants `system.*` perms. |
| 2 | `src/mem_mcp/teams/authz.py` *(new)* | Domain-layer `require_team_permission(conn, *, caller_id, team_id, permission)` with `TeamPermissionDeniedError`. Lazy-imports `has_permission` to keep FastAPI/web.sessions out of the MCP path. |
| 3 | `src/mem_mcp/mcp/tools/_team_authz.py` *(new)* | MCP-layer error envelope mapper: `team_permission_denied_error(err)` → `JsonRpcError(-32603, ..., data={"missing_permission": ...})`, mirroring `_admin_base.AdminTool`. |
| 4 | `src/mem_mcp/mcp/tools/add_team_member.py` | Gate runs as first operation inside `system_tx`, **before** email resolution. Denials use `raise ... from None` (opaque, no existence/enumeration oracle). |
| 5 | `src/mem_mcp/mcp/tools/assign_role.py` | Gate runs as first operation inside `system_tx`, before `assign_role()` which calls `get_role_by_key()`. |
| 6 | `src/mem_mcp/mcp/tools/remove_team_member.py` | Gate runs for non-self removals only. Self-removal (`member_id == ctx.tenant_id`) bypasses the gate; `SoleOwnerCannotSelfRemoveError` still applies as a separate check. |
| 7 | `src/mem_mcp/teams/assignments.py` | `remove_member()` now deletes legacy `team_members` rows for `member_kind='user'` in the same transaction, closing the fallback-path re-grant hole. |
| 8 | `src/mem_mcp/mcp/tool_descriptions.py` | Updated descriptions for all three tools to document the gate, error shape, and oracle properties. |

**Tests (2 new files):**

| File | Tests | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `tests/unit/test_team_role_permissions.py` | 20 | Pure-Python: matrix completeness, namespace disjointness, system/team role matrices, permission set boundaries |
| `tests/security/test_team_membership_authz.py` | 16 (10 cases, 7 parametrized) | DB-backed: positive/negative gate, self-removal bypass, existence oracle, email oracle, legacy revocation, catalog roles, namespace isolation |

### Pre-existing failures (not caused by my changes)

1. **`test_rbac_resolver.py::test_has_permission_inactive_member_denied`** — Inserts `status='invited'` into `team_members`, violating the CHECK constraint `status IN ('active','pending','revoked')`.
2. **`test_effective_access_recompute.py::test_direct_user_member`** / **`test_assign_role_writes_uea_row`** — Assert `path_count == 1` but get `2` (shared DB has leftover `team_members` rows from prior runs).
3. **`test_team_api.py`** (13 tests) — `setup_teams` fixture uses hardcoded emails (`user1@example.com`, `user2@example.com`) that collide with existing rows in the shared DB (`UniqueViolationError`).

### Left open / uncertain

- The `tool_ctx_personal` fixture in `conftest.py` also has a teardown FK issue (deletes `tenants` without first deleting `teams` referencing `created_by_tenant_id`). This is pre-existing and I did not modify it per CLAUDE.md guidance.
- The tenant-scope linter (`tools/lint_tenant_scope.py`) could not be run due to sandbox restrictions, but `teams/authz.py` contains no direct SQL against per-tenant tables (it delegates to `has_permission`), and the `DELETE FROM team_members` in `assignments.py` is scoped to `(team_id, tenant_id)` per the table's PK with `team_members` NOT in `PER_TENANT_TABLES` — so the linter would not flag either file.
- Temporary verification helper files were created and deleted; no trace remains in the repo.
